_about: Oct 6 visual review: every mapped photograph was looked at, both frames, on contact sheets (scripts/exercise-photos/sheets.mjs). Only exercises with a finding are listed. wrong_variant = the photo shows a different exercise or variation and is withdrawn; note = shown as verified, with what a careful viewer should know.

33.note: Clap Push-Up: Plyo_Push-up shows no clap, and is the same photo as Plyo Push-Up (32).

44.note: Pendlay Row: Bent_Over_Barbell_Row keeps the bar hanging; a Pendlay row returns it to the floor each rep.

48.note: Seal Row: Incline_Bench_Pull is on an incline bench; a seal row is prone on a flat, raised bench.

68.note: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up: the Pullups photo is the Pull-Up (66) photo, hands on the angled handles, not palms facing.

69.note: Wide-Grip Pull-Up: the source is titled a rear (behind-the-neck) pull-up, but both frames show a front-facing wide-grip hang and pull; nothing behind the neck is shown. Checked at full size.

93.note: Single-Arm Cable Rear-Delt Fly: at full size one arm pulls and the other rests on the knee (the contact sheet first suggested two arms).

173.note: Bulgarian Split Squat: Split_Squats has the rear foot on the floor; the Bulgarian version elevates it.

203.note: Kettlebell Swing: One-Arm_Kettlebell_Swings is the single-arm swing; the catalog entry is the two-hand swing.

339.note: High Cable Curl: High_Cable_Curls is photographed lying on a bench, not the standing two-pulley curl.

88.note: Rope Face Pull with External Rotation shares the Face_Pull photo; the rope finish at the face is shown.

182.note: Sissy Squat: Weighted_Sissy_Squat shows the lean-back, heels-up sissy squat holding a plate.

184.note: Pistol Squat: Kettlebell_Pistol_Squat holds a kettlebell as counterbalance.

216.note: Lateral Band Walk: Monster_Walk shows the banded wide stance; the direction of travel is not visible in a still.

246.note: RKC Plank: shares the Plank photo; the position is the same, the extra tension is not visible.

395.note: Drop Landing: Linear_Depth_Jump frames show the step off and the landing, not the rebound.
